transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. I guess what finally pushed me to come in is work stuff. I supervise a sales team, and I keep making these stupid mistakes on reports—like I’ll copy the wrong numbers from the team dashboard, or I’ll miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check, even when I really thought I’d gone over it.

And it’s frustrating because it’s not like I don’t care. I’ll sit there and review it, and then later someone points out something obvious. It makes me feel pretty embarrassed, honestly.
Have you had problems with attention or careless mistakes like this since you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, my mom would definitely say yes. She still brings up these notes teachers sent home when I was in elementary school—like that I rushed through my work and missed easy stuff, or I’d lose homework even if I swore I put it in my backpack.

And, I don’t know, she’ll laugh about it now, but at the time it was a whole thing. I’d talk out of turn, get reminded to sit still… I remember my desk being kind of a disaster too—well, maybe that’s not exactly what you asked. But yeah, it wasn’t just something that started at work. It goes way back.
Do these attention problems happen outside of work too?

Yeah, definitely outside work too. It’s not just reports or sales numbers.

I forget regular life stuff all the time—like I’ll mean to call my attorney back and then somehow three days go by. Or I’ll forget to pay a bill until the late notice shows up, and then I’m like, “I swear I was just about to do that.” And with my kids, I’ll tell them I’m going to pick something up for them, and then I get home and realize I completely forgot.

It’s embarrassing, because it’s small stuff, but it adds up.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah, I do. Especially if it’s a long meeting or something where I’m supposed to just sit there and listen. It’s like my body is buzzing on the inside, if that makes sense.

I’ll keep shifting in the chair, tapping my foot, messing with a pen… and then I start thinking about whether everyone can see me doing it, which somehow makes it worse. Sometimes I’ll make up a reason to step out, like I need water or have to check on something, just so I can move around for a minute.
Have these attention problems caused significant difficulties in more than one area of your life, such as work, home, or relationships?

Yeah… more than one area, for sure. At work it’s gotten serious enough that my manager actually put it in a formal review, which was pretty humiliating. It wasn’t just like, “try to be more organized,” it was written down as a problem.

And then at home—sorry, I’m trying not to ramble—but at home it causes fights because people feel like they can’t count on me to follow through. Like if I say I’ll handle something, there’s this look like, “Are you actually going to?” And I get why they feel that way, but it still feels awful.
